core_claim.quote: a fundamental tenet of HOT is that first-order states occur unconsciously, and are not sufficient for phenomenally conscious experiences to occur

source.citation: Brown R, Lau H, LeDoux JE. Understanding the higher-order approach to consciousness. Trends in Cognitive Sciences 23(9):754-768, 2019. Quoted from the authors' preprint: Brown R, Lau H, LeDoux JE. The misunderstood higher-order approach to consciousness. PsyArXiv, 2019 (doi 10.31234/osf.io/xpy8h)

prediction.statement: Activity in sensory cortex that carries a stimulus, including activity fed back within sensory cortex, can occur while the person does not experience the stimulus; sensory activity alone does not make an experience.

first_stated.passage: For example, when self-reports of the stimulus are compromised by using subliminal stimulation procedures, such as masking (63), areas of the visual cortex (including primary and secondary areas) are functionally active, but when participants are able to consciously report seeing a visual stimulus, additional cortical areas become active

source.citation: LeDoux JE, Brown R. A higher-order theory of emotional consciousness. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 114(10):E2016-E2025, 2017

prediction.test_for: Stimulus-specific activity in sensory cortex, including feedback (recurrent) activity between sensory areas, is found on trials where the person reports no experience of the stimulus and cannot tell it apart from no stimulus.
prediction.test_against: Whenever feedback activity between sensory areas carrying a stimulus is present, the person experiences the stimulus, and whenever it is absent they do not, with no further area needed to predict experience.

what_the_sources_say_about_rivals.statement: Recurrent processing theory holds that feedback between visual areas is enough for experience, with nothing beyond visual cortex needed.

source.citation: Lamme VAF. Challenges for theories of consciousness: seeing or knowing, the missing ingredient and how to deal with it. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 373:20170344, 2018

other_statements_of_the_prediction.passage: In contrast, David Rosenthal and other higher-order theorists argue that a first-order state resulting from stimulus-processing alone is not enough to make possible the conscious experience of a stimulus

source.citation: LeDoux JE, Brown R. A higher-order theory of emotional consciousness. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 114(10):E2016-E2025, 2017

other_statements_of_the_prediction.passage: It is known that subliminal or unconscious stimulation also engages similar sensory circuits as consciously experienced stimuli [76]. Also, ongoing spontaneous activity in the very same neurons giving rise to normal perception is typical unconscious [77]. One possibility is that such activity has to reach a certain threshold [59], or that it has to achieve a right sort of dynamic profile [58, 77], such as involving feedback to V1. But patients with damage to V1 can still have visual experiences [18, 78].
